probe: the docker socket is there and the daemon behind it answers /_ping. All three are different failures and the probe separates them: no socket is a host with no docker, a socket this process may not open is a group the unit was not given, and a socket nobody answers is a daemon that is down or a stale file a crash left behind. A host running docker with nothing started still answers, and that is a reading of zero containers rather than a probe failure

collections.name: containers
collections.question: what is running on this host under docker, how do I reach it, and which stack does it belong to?

State.sentence: Where dockerd says this container is, in docker's own word for it. `running` is the only positively healthy one; `exited` is a container that finished, which is neutral until the exit code says otherwise, and `restarting`, `paused` and `dead` each mean a container that exists and is not doing its job.

Status.sentence: Docker's own human sentence about the state, which carries what the listing endpoint otherwise omits: how long it has been up, the exit code it stopped with, and whether its healthcheck is failing. It is the only place on a row where an exit code or a health verdict appears at all, because the listing document has neither as a member.

Image.sentence: The image reference this container was created from, as the operator wrote it. A bare tag says which image, never which build — the tag moves when the registry does — so a container running `latest` and a container running the digest it resolved to look identical here and are not.

Created.sentence: When this container object was created, which is not when it last started: a container recreated by a deploy gets a new time, and one that has been restarted a hundred times keeps its old one. Rendered from the listing's epoch seconds as UTC.

ComposeProject.sentence: The compose project this container belongs to, from the label compose writes on everything it creates. It is the cross-subsystem edge to the compose-stack-<project>.service unit that manages it, and it is what turns eight unrelated container rows into two stacks. Absent means nothing generated by compose created this container, which is the ordinary shape for anything started by hand.

NetworkMode.sentence: The container's network namespace as docker runs it: a bridge or network name means ports reach it only via published mappings, while "host" means it shares the host's stack — every port the process binds is open on the host's own addresses, which is why such a row carries no Ports fact.

ContainerID.sentence: The first twelve characters of the container id, which is the form docker itself shows and the form every host-side row carries. The NAME is the object's id here, not this, because a compose service keeps its name across recreations while the id changes every time. Minted from randomness at create time, so it denotes nothing outside the daemon that minted it.

ScopeUnit.sentence: The systemd unit the container's processes run in while it has any, which is where the host keeps their resource accounting: the kernel measures CPU, memory and I/O pressure per cgroup, and this scope is the container's. The name is derived from the container id, so it is also the way back — a host-side row named for a hexadecimal id and nothing else becomes this container. Absent on a stopped container, whose scope systemd deleted with its last process.

Ports.sentence: How to reach the container from the host network: each entry maps a published host address and port to the container port behind it, and a port marked (exposed) was never published, so it is reachable only from other containers. Absent where the container publishes and exposes nothing at all, which is different from a container on host networking — read NetworkMode to tell those apart.

collections.name: volumes
collections.question: what named storage does docker hold on this host, and which stack owns it?

Driver.sentence: Which volume driver holds this volume. `local` is a directory on this host's filesystem and is what almost every volume is; anything else is a plugin, and the data is somewhere this collector cannot see.

Mountpoint.sentence: Where on this host's filesystem the volume's data actually sits. It is the answer to "what do I back up" and to "what is filling this disk", which no other fact on the row gives — the volume's name says nothing about where its bytes are.

ComposeProject.sentence: The compose project that created this volume, from the label compose writes on everything it creates. Absent means nothing generated by compose created it — which, for a volume, is also the shape a volume left behind by a deleted stack has.

collections.name: networks
collections.question: what networks does docker run on this host, and which host interface is each one plumbed onto?

Driver.sentence: Which docker network driver runs this network. `bridge` is a real host bridge with a real device behind it; `host` shares the host's own stack and plumbs nothing; `null` is docker's word for the network that attaches a container to no network at all. The last two are on every daemon and cannot be removed.

Scope.sentence: How far this network reaches: `local` means it exists on this host only, which is every network on a daemon that is not in a swarm. A `swarm` or `global` scope means the network is defined across a cluster, and this host is showing one member of it.

Internal.sentence: Whether docker withholds external routing from this network. An internal network's containers can reach each other and nothing beyond the host, which is a deliberate isolation and reads as a fault to anyone who does not know it was chosen.

BridgeInterface.sentence: The host device this network is plumbed onto, which is what joins a docker network to the interface rows the host publishes. Docker names it explicitly for the default bridge (docker0) and for every other bridge network it is `br-` plus the first twelve characters of the network id — so a `br-56a84c7a9838` row in the host's link list stops being anonymous plumbing and becomes a named stack's network. Absent for the host and null drivers, which plumb no device at all.

ComposeProject.sentence: The compose project that created this network, from the label compose writes on everything it creates. Absent on docker's own three default networks, which no compose file made and no compose file can remove.
